title: Rey's Perfect Paper Boat Parade
markdown:
Young Rey, who kept an eye on the sky for the village, had a brand-new idea one blustery afternoon. It wasn’t about clouds at all. It was about the brook that giggled its way towards Nana Tess's prize petunias.

"A paper boat parade!" Rey announced, already folding paper faster than a hummingbird’s wings. Saffron, Rey's parrot, a magnificent splash of rainbow feathers, puffed out his chest and squawked, "Parade! Parade! Rey's parade!"

Rey launched the first boat, a neat little tugboat. *Splish, splash!* It bobbed for a second, a tiny white explorer. Then, *gurgle, gulp,* it took a big drink and sank like a soggy sock! "Oh no!" Rey cried. Saffron shrieked, "Sank! Sank! Soggy boat!" Rey grabbed another piece of paper, folding a wider boat. It wiggled and jiggled, but soon it too surrendered to the stream's pull. Rey's shoulders drooped. It felt like a sinking disaster. "It's no use," Rey sighed, a little puff of frustration escaping.

Just then, Nana Tess appeared. Her smile was as bright as spring daffodils. "What's all this gloom, Rey?" she asked, her voice soft as a favourite blanket. Rey pointed at the wet paper bits. "My boats keep sinking, Nana Tess," Rey explained. "They're not having a parade, they're having a swim lesson!"

Nana Tess knelt beside Rey. "Hmm," she hummed, a thoughtful sound. "A puzzle, isn't it? What if we try changing just *one* thing at a time to see what happens? That's how we learn, you know."

Rey looked puzzled. "One change? But I want them to be the best!" Saffron tilted his head. "One change! One change! Smart, smart!"

Nana Tess picked up a fresh piece of paper. "Let's make this boat like your first one," she said, creasing and folding with quick fingers. "Identical. Now," she continued, her voice full of adventure, "let's add just one tiny pebble to the bottom." She carefully placed a small stone inside. Together, they launched it. *Whoosh!* That boat didn't just sink; it zipped down the stream like a tiny submarine and vanished! "See that, Rey?" Nana Tess beamed. "By adding just that pebble, it sank much quicker! That tells us something!"

Rey's eyes widened, bright with a new kind of excitement. This was a puzzle! "So," Rey asked, leaning forward, "if adding a pebble makes it sink faster, what happens if we don't add a pebble? What if we try making the sail on another boat a little bit smaller?" Quickly, Rey folded a new boat, but this time, Rey creased the main sail flat, so it wouldn't catch so much wind. They launched it with a hopeful flick. *Whoosh! Glide!* The little boat sailed smoothly, dancing on the water. With a final curve, it reached the edge of Nana Tess's bright pond. "Hooray!" Saffron shrieked, flapping his wings with delight.

Rey was buzzing now, a whirl of ideas. "We need them lighter! And smaller sails!" Rey exclaimed, reaching for more paper. They worked together in a happy flurry: paper rustling, quick folds, Saffron's excited squawks. One boat had a tiny bit of weight removed from its base. Another had its sail trimmed. They even made one hull more pointed, like a tiny arrowhead. Each time, they launched a boat and watched its journey, learning from every wobble and glide.

Finally, there it was: a fleet! A fleet of triumphant paper boats. Rey held them up proudly. "Look, Nana Tess!" Rey exclaimed, beaming. "We changed only one thing at a time to see what worked best!" With a cheer, they launched the whole fleet. *Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh!* The paper boats sailed down the stream, bobbing merrily, their sails catching the breeze just right. They reached Nana Tess's pond, one after another, a perfect, glorious paper boat parade!

Nana Tess watched, her smile radiating pride. "You see, Rey?" she said softly. "By changing only one thing at a time, you made a fair test. You could see how each small change made a difference. That's how we learn to predict what will happen!" Rey felt a huge, warm swell of pride. They hadn't just sent boats down a stream; they had discovered the amazing power of experimenting. "Wow!" Rey breathed, a sense of wonder washing over them. "This is so much fun! What else can we test?" Saffron ruffled his feathers and squawked happily, "More tests! More tests! Best parade ever!"
characters: Rey the weather watcher, Saffron the parrot, Nana Tess
